annotations.title: List, add or remove a track's scheduled fetches

description: For a service that has the data but never sends it (a social network's post stats, a shop's stock, an API with no webhooks): every 1, 3, 6, 12 or 24 hours TrackerHacker asks an address and the track's JSON or text hacks read the answer exactly like a webhook body, a list making one row per item. The same answer twice in a day writes nothing, so for a daily history give the schema's row key keyPer day (publish_schema). action list shows a track's fetches (never their address or tokens); add takes label, url (public https), everyHours and token, and runs it once before keeping it (a failing one isn't kept; its rows come back as rows); run runs one now; set_token replaces a token the service refused, which had paused it, or its refresh; remove takes one away. The token is sent as Authorization: Bearer. A fetch can be a POST with a JSON body (method, body) and send up to 6 headers of its own (an API version, say). The url and body can name days, filled in the person's timezone as YYYY-MM-DD: {today}, {yesterday}, {days_ago:7}. A token that runs out can be renewed by TrackerHacker (refresh): style oauth trades a refresh token at tokenUrl with the person's own app's clientId and clientSecret (clientIdName for a service that calls it something else, like client_key; clientAuth basic for one that wants them as Basic auth), with or without a token to start; style renew sends the current long-lived token to tokenUrl before it runs out. Take tokens and secrets only when the person gives them to you for this, treat them like passwords, and never repeat them back. Build the hack from what the first run put in the Inbox (read_inbox).

body.description: add: a POST's JSON body, as an object or JSON text. May name {today}, {yesterday} or {days_ago:N}.

fetchId.description: run, set_token, remove: from action list.

headers.description: add: up to 6 headers of the fetch's own, like {"LinkedIn-Version": "202611"}. Not Authorization, Content-Type, Accept or Cookie.

label.description: add: what it fetches, like "Instagram posts".

refresh.description: add, set_token: how TrackerHacker renews the token.

clientAuth.description: oauth: send the client id and secret in the form (default) or as Basic auth.

clientId.description: oauth: the person's own app's client id.

clientIdName.description: oauth: the form field for the client id, when not client_id (TikTok: client_key).

tokenUrl.description: The service's https address that gives new tokens.

token.description: add, set_token: the service's access token, sent as a bearer token. Leave out when the address carries its own key, or when refresh gets the first one.

url.description: add: the https address to GET, with its query (fields, limit). An API key may ride in it, like YouTube's key=.
